relevance_note: Case report of HA20 with individual-level detail: the proband carries "a heterozygous c.A1939C (NM_001270508) p.T647P variant in TNFAIP3", and a second family has "heterozygous p.N98Tfs25 TNFAIP3-associated autoinflammation".
method_note: Read the full text (including the Online Repository section with Table E1) directly; no script was used, so no stacked-cell (' / ') cells were encountered. In-scope people: subject III.1, her sister III.2, her mother II.2 (all carrying the p.T647P variant), her relative II.4 (deceased, described in relation to in-scope people), and the two p.N98Tfs25 carriers of the second family (an unnamed 4-year-old boy and his father), who have no printed labels, so labels 'unnamed person 1' and 'father of unnamed person 1' were created. publications.n_patients_reported = 5; cohort_size_as_stated is null because the authors never state a study total. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false with no span, since the paper makes no statement about earlier publication of its own patients. Reference [2] (Aeschlimann, PMID:29317407) is quoted only as a cohort-level frequency ('CNS vasculitis was reported in 2 (13%) of 16 patients with HA20'), which gives no individual-level detail, so no rows were created for those patients. Contradiction found: III.1 presented with 'left-sided focal seizures' but after baricitinib has 'no further seizures'; seizures are not a checklist item, so the phenotypic row records the presentation statement and the checklist is unaffected. III.1's 'no history of systemic symptoms' was recorded as a phenotypic feature only. Table E1 (single data column, subject III.1) was used for the autoantibody finding; its other laboratory values were left out because the paper does not label them abnormal or normal for a checklist item. D-27 normal findings were recorded as the abnormality ruled out (elevated C-reactive protein, positive autoantibody screen, abnormal complement function). Spans for evidence_basis repeat the span of the feature they describe. For the composite checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' in III.1 I recorded observed, because her ESR was increased while her CRP was normal; the two separate phenotypic_features rows keep the ESR observed and the CRP normal. The father of the second family's boy has no label of his own in the paper, so the relative label 'father of unnamed person 1' was used. Subject II.1 appears only once, in the Methods ('family members (subject II.1)'), with no individual-level fact beyond being a tested family member; II.1 and II.4 have no TNFAIP3 variant attributed to them, so they have no variants row, while n_patients_reported counts only the five people the paper ties to a TNFAIP3 variant.
